You own the HEART OF THE PRODUCT: the AI builder. Take the time to do this properly.

READ FIRST, in this order — binding contract:
1. `docs/design-system.md` — tokens, components, and an AUDITED table of what does NOT exist.
2. `app/globals.css` — the "KODELY PRODUCT SURFACE" and "PRODUCT UTILITIES" blocks. Note `k-preview-busy`/`k-preview-idle`, `k-msg-in`, `k-step-*`.
3. `components/ui/*` — the primitives, especially `AIProgress` + `stepsAt`, `Segmented`, `Menu`, `Modal`, `Badge`, `Button`. Import them; never hand-roll a second version.
4. Then the builder itself, in full: `app/projects/[id]/page.tsx`, `Editor.tsx` (1634 lines — read all of it), `PreviewFrame.tsx`, `BuildingOverlay.tsx`, `BuildInterrupted.tsx`, `BuildRating.tsx`, `CommandPalette.tsx`, `CostEstimate.tsx`, `DiffView.tsx`, `SelectionPanel.tsx`, `SeoPanel.tsx`, `diff.ts`, `diff-actions.ts`, `preview-agent.ts`.
5. `app/api/generate/route.ts` IN FULL — you must know its exact SSE event vocabulary.

YOU OWN: everything under `app/projects/[id]/`. Do NOT touch `app/(portal)/**`, `components/ui/**`, `components/app/**`, or `lib/**`. If you need a change in a shared primitive, report it to me instead of editing it.

The builder deliberately sits OUTSIDE the portal shell — it is full-bleed chat + preview, and a 248px nav rail would eat a fifth of the customer's preview. It carries its own back-to-dashboard affordance. Keep it that way, but make it unmistakably the same product: same tokens, same components, same motion.

## THE TARGET LAYOUT

LEFT: AI chat / prompt panel. RIGHT: live website preview occupying most of the screen. Conversation + live website. That is the core Kodely experience.

## 1. CHAT PANEL

Must feel like an assistant, not a textarea. Header "Kodely AI" with a real status (Ready / Working / Error) using `Badge` with `dot` and `pulse`. Conversation history, input pinned at the bottom, placeholder "Ask Kodely to change anything…". Suggested follow-up prompts that change with context.

Support, only where real: conversation history, follow-ups, regenerate, undo, retry after failure, stop generation, attach image. **Check each against the code before you build a control for it.** Image attach is real (`app/api/generate/route.ts` accepts only `data:image/png|jpeg|webp;base64`, attempt 1 only). Non-image file upload does NOT exist — no multipart, no object storage. If "stop generation" cannot actually abort the server-side run, then either wire it to a real abort or do not offer a button that only hides the UI.

## 2. AI PROGRESS — THE MOST IMPORTANT PART

When a change is submitted, the preview must not just sit there while something happens invisibly.

- Preview goes to `k-preview-busy` (a mild blur — the customer must still recognise their own site underneath, or it reads as replaced rather than edited) with a Kodely progress treatment over it.
- The chat panel simultaneously shows `AIProgress` with the same steps in the same states.
- On completion the preview transitions smoothly back and the chat shows the change applied.

**NON-NEGOTIABLE:** the steps must be driven by REAL signals from the generate SSE stream. A timer walking the list forward is a fake and will sit on "Finalizing" long after a build has failed. Read `app/api/generate/route.ts` in full, enumerate its actual events, and map steps onto them. **If the stream cannot distinguish a phase, show fewer truthful steps rather than more invented ones.** Report the real event vocabulary and exactly how faithful your mapping is. Note `lib/build-narration.ts` already exists — check whether it is the intended source of this text.

## 3. PREVIEW

Make it feel like a real browser: URL, desktop/tablet/mobile toggle, refresh, open in new tab, zoom, fullscreen. It must stay fully interactive — read `PreviewFrame.tsx:17-26` for why it is a `srcdoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"` and no `allow-same-origin`, and do not break that. Note the draft preview has NO working forms by design (`app/api/preview/[id]/[[...path]]/route.ts:46-50`) — do not add a "test your form" affordance that cannot work. "Open in new tab" must point at something that genuinely resolves; work out what that is for a draft vs a published site and say so.

## 4. EVERY STATE, DESIGNED

Empty (no site yet) · Building (initial) · Ready · Updating · Success · Error · Publishing · Published. Each gets deliberate UI. `BuildInterrupted.tsx` already handles one of these — understand it before replacing it.

## 5. VERSION HISTORY

Real and already built: checkpoints (`app/api/projects/[id]/builds/route.ts`), restore (`.../restore/route.ts`), and a real line diff (`diff.ts`, `DiffView.tsx`). Surface it properly — version, time, what changed, view / restore / compare.

**Two truths the UI must carry:** snapshots are PRUNED (kept only for the newest 20 per project, and only those older than 30 days are eligible — see `lib/retention.ts:65,74`), so history is bounded and the list must keep filtering on snapshot survival. And restoring does not refund credits or cancel anything. The existing DiffView already states some of this honestly — preserve that honesty, do not smooth it away.

## 6. MOBILE

Carefully designed, not a shrunk desktop. Chat and preview cannot share a phone screen — decide the interaction (tabs? sheet? swap?) and justify it.

HARD RULES:
- `k-focus` on every interactive element, `k-num` on figures, `k-scroll-x` on wide blocks.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (globals.css already neutralises blur for it).
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings. Run both and fix everything.
- Comment like the rest of this codebase: explain WHY, especially where you rejected an approach.

REPORT BACK: what you built, the REAL SSE vocabulary and how faithfully your steps map to it, every control you considered and did NOT build because it would have been fake, your mobile decision and its justification, and anything untested — say untested rather than overstating.

18	// every read by `project.userId`, exactly as the sibling REST routes do. A
19	// build id belonging to someone else's project must be indistinguishable from
20	// one that does not exist, which is why both fall out of the same query and
21	// share one message.
22	//
23	// SIZE. `filesSnapshot` is roughly 105 kB per build (lib/retention.ts), and this
24	// reads two of them — but only the diff crosses back to the browser, and
25	// diff.ts bounds that. The snapshots themselves never leave the server.
26	
27	type Snapshot = { source?: Record<string, string>; build?: Record<string, string> };
28	
29	/**
30	 * The file-level changes one successful build made, against the newest earlier
31	 * checkpoint whose snapshot still exists.
32	 *
33	 * Compares the SOURCE tree, not the compiled build output: source is what the
34	 * Code view shows, what the agent edits, and what the user means by "my files".
35	 * The compiled tree would diff on every build regardless of whether anything
36	 * meaningful changed.
37	 *
38	 * Never throws for an expected condition — a thrown Server Action surfaces to
39	 * the client as an opaque "an error occurred", which is useless for the two
40	 * conditions that actually happen here (a pruned snapshot, a stale build id).
41	 */
42	export async function loadBuildDiff(
43	  projectId: string,
44	  buildId: string,
45	): Promise<BuildDiffResult> {
46	  const user = await getCurrentUser();
47	  if (!user) return { ok: false, error: "Not signed in." };
48	
49	  const build = await db.build.findFirst({
50	    where: { id: buildId, projectId, status: "SUCCEEDED", project: { userId: user.id } },
51	    select: {
52	      id: true,
53	      prompt: true,
54	      createdAt: true,
55	      filesWritten: true,
56	      filesSnapshot: true,
57	    },
58	  });
59	  if (!build) return { ok: false, error: "That build could not be found." };
60	  if (!build.filesSnapshot) {
61	    // The row survives, the snapshot does not. Distinct from "not found", and
62	    // the difference matters to the user: nothing is broken and nothing is
63	    // lost from the live draft — an old checkpoint was simply reclaimed.
64	    return {
65	      ok: false,
66	      error:
67	        "The file snapshot for this build has been cleared to save storage, so its changes can no longer be shown.",
68	    };
69	  }
70	
71	  // The newest earlier build whose snapshot survives. Ordering by createdAt
72	  // mirrors the checkpoint list (app/api/projects/[id]/builds/route.ts) so the
73	  // "previous" here is the same row the History panel shows directly above.
74	  const previous = await db.build.findFirst({
75	    where: {
76	      projectId,
77	      status: "SUCCEEDED",
78	      createdAt: { lt: build.createdAt },
79	      filesSnapshot: { not: Prisma.DbNull },
80	    },
81	    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
82	    select: { id: true, prompt: true, createdAt: true, filesSnapshot: true },
83	  });
84	
85	  // Was there an earlier build at all? Only asked when `previous` came back
86	  // empty, so the common path pays nothing for it. This is what separates "the
87	  // first build of this project" from "the earlier checkpoint was pruned" —
88	  // two situations that produce an identical-looking whole-tree diff and must
89	  // not be described to the user in the same words.
90	  const previousPruned =
91	    previous === null &&
92	    (await db.build.count({
93	      where: { projectId, status: "SUCCEEDED", createdAt: { lt: build.createdAt } },
94	    })) > 0;
95	
96	  const after = (build.filesSnapshot as Snapshot).source ?? {};
97	  const before = previous ? ((previous.filesSnapshot as Snapshot).source ?? {}) : {};
98	
99	  return {

101	    diff: {
102	      build: {
103	        id: build.id,
104	        prompt: build.prompt,
105	        createdAt: build.createdAt.toISOString(),
106	        filesWritten: build.filesWritten,
107	      },
108	      previous: previous
109	        ? {
110	            id: previous.id,
111	            prompt: previous.prompt,
112	            createdAt: previous.createdAt.toISOString(),
113	          }
114	        : null,
115	      previousPruned,
116	      files: diffTrees(before, after),
117	    },
118	  };
